dod_intent_evidence: DARPA SBIR Phase II ($1,746,406, 2023) for 'mSense: Mobile & Wearable Sensing at scale' whose own abstract states the goal is to 'continuously monitor warfighter health and readiness at the edge in real-time' — genuine DoD motion, though absent from the public-facing homepage entirely.
score_evidence: 'Deliver Digital Biomarker Innovation with a deep scientific data analysis of the data collection' — commercial clinical-trial marketing language with no operational/field framing → lab_language_intensity

SBIR abstract describes edge processing and battery constraints in technical detail with zero ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR/DDIL language (capped at 12: own-language word count ~765, under 1000) → deployment_awareness_absence

'continuously monitor warfighter health and readiness at the edge' is the only warfighter/operator mention across the entire pack; no training, CONOPS, or field feedback discussed (capped at 12) → operator_absence
No jobs data in pack ('Open roles: (no jobs data found)') → hiring_profile_skew set exactly 10 per instructions
Homepage copyright reads '© 2019-2023 thinksense' (stale site), company still at 3-4 employees off a single DARPA SBIR Phase II → stage_pressure

blind_spots.blind_spot: Public commercial website never mentions the DARPA-funded warfighter application at all — it frames the entire product as a civilian clinical-trial/HIPAA platform
blind_spots.operator_reality: A go-to-market message that omits the military use case entirely suggests the defense application still lives only inside a $1.75M SBIR abstract, not in an actual fielding plan — there is no visible bridge from 'digital biomarkers for drug development' to 'a device a warfighter wears on patrol.'
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The commercial clinical-trials business (cohort data collection, HIPAA compliance) is clearly the company's primary go-to-market identity; the DARPA award appears to be a separate, unintegrated research track.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'Digital biomarker sensing technologies... HIPPA compliant... Focus on mental and behavioral health & drug development' (homepage) vs. 'continuously monitor warfighter health and readiness at the edge' (SBIR abstract)

blind_spots.blind_spot: SBIR abstract shows real battery/SWaP awareness ('less than 5% of the wearable battery over 10 days') but assumes periodic connectivity rather than full DDIL denial
blind_spots.operator_reality: A warfighter on an extended patrol in a comms-denied environment needs the wearable to function and store data fully offline for days — the abstract's language of 'minimize the data transmission' implies incremental transmission is still expected, not the total denial that a DDIL environment can impose.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The proposal's framing comes from a wellness/telehealth mental model (continuous light transmission to a backend) rather than a tactical-edge mental model (store-and-forward under total denial).
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'By running the models at the edge, the platform can reduce latency, minimize the data transmission, and real-time feedback to the user.'

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention of who on a unit trains on or interprets mSense outputs, and no CMMC/ITAR framing despite HIPAA being explicitly claimed for the civilian product
blind_spots.operator_reality: Physiological/behavioral-health data collected on a warfighter's body is sensitive PII/PHI in a military context that HIPAA alone does not cover — without a visible CMMC/ITAR plan, this data-handling gap is likely to surface the moment the DARPA prototype tries to move toward a unit-level pilot.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Compliance language on the site is entirely civilian-clinical-trial-oriented (HIPAA), suggesting the team has not yet built out the parallel government-data-handling compliance track.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'HIPPA compliant' (as the sole compliance claim on the site, alongside a DARPA warfighter-health SBIR with no CMMC/ITAR mention)

opener_hook: ThinkSense's DARPA SBIR Phase II ($1.75M, 2023) targets continuous warfighter health monitoring at the edge, though the company's public site frames itself entirely as a civilian clinical-trial platform.
what_they_do: Digital biomarker/wearable-sensor data platform (mSense) built for civilian clinical trials and drug development, with a DARPA SBIR track applying the same edge-sensing tech to continuous warfighter health monitoring.
